INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  Library Board
  MINUTES – October 27, 2021

The Inglewood Library Board met on October 27, 2021 via Zoom. The meeting was called to order at 4:30 p.m. by
Board Member Julie Minton.

Roll Call

Present:
  Patt Sanders – At Large Board Member, Chairman
  Julie Minton – District 1 Board Member, Vice Chairman
  Pat Douglas – District 2 Board Member
  Ernesto Castillo – District 3 Board Member
  Jacqueline Cochran – District 4 Board Member

Staff:
  Harjinder Singh – Deputy to the City Manager
  Kerri Arroyo – Library Manager
  Irina Martirosian – Staff Assistant

Public Comments

  None

Approval of the Minutes

  Board Member Minton made a motion for the approval of the minutes for September 22, 2021
  Board Member Douglas seconded the motion. Minutes were approved as follows:

  Ayes: Library Board Members Douglas, Cochran and Castillo
  Nays: None

  Due to Thanksgiving and Christmas holidays, Deputy to the City Manager, Harjinder Singh asked the board
to discuss the Holiday schedule.

  Board Member Cochran made a motion for Board Members to have a Special Meeting on November 17,
2021 and to suspend the December regular Board Meeting until January 2022. Board Member Minton seconded
the motion. Motion was approved as follows:

  Ayes: Library Board Members Minton, Sanders, Douglas and Castillo
  Nays: None

Library Report

  1
 Deputy to the City Manager, Harjinder Singh gave the board members Library’s update on library
reorganization that was approved by the Mayor and City Council, staffing and all the benefits that library is
going to get from the changes that have been made. A number of Library positions were added and
unfrozen. Instead of 3 full time associate librarians now we will have 9 full time associate librarian positions.
Also, principal librarian positions have been eliminated and upgraded to Assistant Library Manager
Positions. Instead of having 4 principal librarians now we have 2 assistant Library Managers and combine
technical services and adult services together, and children’s Services and extension services together.
The balance of the money from those positions paid for the new and upgraded positions that we are looking
to hire. We added a senior library support supervisor position that oversees 4 library support supervisors
that oversee the 4 different sections of the library, circulation, computers, book intake and Crenshaw
library. Also, our Courier position was permanent part time and we changed that to full time position. All
those structural changes and hiring are being made to deliver the highest amount of customer service
possible.

Board member Minton asked a question about hiring full time librarians, if library is still hiring in a trial basis,
how does that work and if the positions are going to be internally filled or open to the public?
Deputy to the City Manager, Harjinder Singh explained the hiring procedure.
Board member Cochran asked if library is going to hire another supervisor for Morningside Branch after
opening.
Deputy to the City Manager, Harjinder Singh told board that one of our supervisors will be working at the
Morningside Branch after opening. Mr. Singh also informed the board that the budget was approved for 1.7
million dollars for renovation of the 2600 sq. foot Morningside Library, shared the floor plan and stated that
Morningside library is going to be more of a digital library and for class visits.

Deputy to the City Manager, Harjinder Singh told board members that on top of the blast that is going out
weekly, fine free advertising also will be running on all the billboards in the city and every patron record has
zero balance now.

Library Manager, Kerri Arroyo gave the board members Library’s update on programming, internship, class
visits, outreach programs, none credit collage classes and accomplishments. Shared pictures of pumpkin
curving which we had on a site at the Main Library and outreach program at the park, bilingual story time
program that takes place once a month on Saturdays and gardening. Non-credit college classes that we
offer to adult special needs and teens at Crenshaw library have 10 students who come on site and 11
students who attend virtually. We have 1 intern from UCLA, he’s here for the fall and 2 more will come on
spring of 2022. 1 more candidate is interested in internship from South Carolina. Our intern Anders started
20 ft. long and 5 ft. tall movable canvas program. He brings all the ages together. That also gives High
school student’s opportunity to do community service. They are painting a mural that will live in our library.
Children’s librarian is having tremendous success in class visits. She’s seen 139 students virtually and on
site.

Board member Douglas asked where is that large canvas located and if anyone can participate?
Library Manager, Kerri Arroyo told board that the canvas is rolled up and when it’s time for painting it’s
taken outside and laying on painters’ cloth. All the participants are on the ground on comfortable blankets
and anyone can participate. All the participants are having fun and it’s very exciting.

  2
 Friends Report

  None

Public Comments

  None

Commissioner Comments

  Board member Douglas was very pleased with the progress. Appreciated Deputy to the City Manager,
  Harjinder Singh and staff for fantastic work.
  Board member Cochran also was delighted with the report, fabulous job that was done with the
  reorganization and planning, she’s telling everyone about grab and go, people see changes when they
  come to the library and are very happy. Board member Cochran also mentioned that one of her friends call
  and complained about parking on the Game day, Monday.
  Deputy to the City Manager, Harjinder Singh told the board that he’s been working closely with the parking
  group on a regular basis and they understand that the library operations come first and we can get as many
  parking spaces as we need and city is fully supportive of that.
  Board member Minton asked about Library director’s position and the role of the board.
  Deputy to the City Manager, Harjinder Singh explained that the current reorganization plan did not require a
  Director and the current positions outlined in the plan will be sufficient to accomplish the goals of the library.
  Deputy to the City Manager, Harjinder Singh reiterated that the library head is the Library Manager Ms.
  Kerri Arroyo as he oversees various areas in the City. Information was provided stating that the board
  operates in an advisory capacity.
  Chairman Sanders was excited about all changes, community involvement, but concerned about how the
  commission is not included, not being used in any process of making decision.
  With no further comments the meeting was adjourned at 5:34 p.m.
